- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; increase early-term lows and avoid extreme negative forecasts.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., 30d forecast spikes > 10x true outcome), suggesting momentum bias; cap forecast peaks at 2x recent high or 1.5x prior 7d average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast is >1.5x true outcome for 3 consecutive days, reduce by 20–40% unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- Sentiment history with alternating +/– signals (e.g., 0.33, 1.00, 0.33) suggests model overfits short-term noise; dampen forecast volatility in such regimes.
- If sentiment is flat (0.33–0.67) for 5+ days, model tends to drift toward over-optimistic forecasts; apply downward bias of 10–25% to 30d mean.
- Avoid forecasting extreme outliers (e.g., >5x true outcome) unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.80) and recent price is rising; otherwise, cap at 3x recent 7d average.
